full_judgment: 10. Mr Mahmudul Islam, learned Advocate for the petitioners in Civil Petition Nos. 198-204 of 1996, submits that the language of regulations 18(C) of Biman's Service Regulations being clear and unambiguous and the expression "from the date an employee satisfactorily completes his training" clearly showing that the seniority of an employee should be counted from the date he actually completes his training, the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the date of completion will not mean the actual date on which an employee completes his training but a subsequent notional date, that is, the date on which training of the last batch was completed. Secondly, Mr. Islam submits that in the absence of any proper pleading showing that the selection of candidates for training in three batches was arbitrary or discriminatory, the High Court Division was wrong in holding that the placement of the candidates in the three batches of training was arbitrary and discriminatory. Lastly, Mr. Islam has submitted that the burden of proving discrimination being on the person who alleges it and the writ-petitioners having not pleaded any facts or circumstances showing discrimination, the High Court Division ought to have held that the presumption of validity of classification has not been rebutted.
